title: Review of c18's food-cogs (SIBE): replicated on fresh seed 5 - 11 shelled cogs from noise (shell/trough 22.8), the isolated cog dies by t=650 after its food is cut at t=600 while its fed twin stays at 1.00 and other bodies are unaffected; removing k4 spills the shell into a labyrinth
summary: Verdict written before reading other reviews. On new seed 5 I ran c18's world.py and scripts unchanged: a labkit pack to t=1000, radial_cog.py on its frames, runsave.py to t=600, mkcut.py (most isolated cog at y=19 x=108, nearest other core 53 px), 300 t of fed twin and local cut (CUT=1, r=18), cutplot.py, and the shell-source ablation k4=0 on the t=600 state for 100 t. From full-domain noise (sheet t=0) cogs form by t~85 and 11 persist to t=1000 (11 tracks alive >= 50% of the run). Shell profile over 67 isolated cell-frames: A1 0.875 at r=8 vs 0.038 in the trough at r=4 and 0.017 outside (shell/trough 22.8, shell/outside 52; per-cell minimum 0.52). Local cut (localcut_s5.txt): the cut cog falls below 10% at t=650 and is gone by t=900 while the same cog in the fed twin stays at 1.00; all other bodies 0.923 in both runs. k4=0: A1 total 2474 -> 15973 within 25 t (k4_ablation_s5.txt), cores persist (A0 1063 -> 1120).

verdicts.limitation: E holds by construction (matter built only from food, decay 0.002); the fork shows the cog collapses after a small deficit, far sooner than its stock would last. After t~400 the population is static: cogs neither move, divide nor die while fed, so this is metabolism of frozen individuals, not turnover. The cut disk is a permanent sink. One new seed; I did not run dt/2 or a resolution test of the 4-5 px shell.
